paper.title: DINCAE 2.0: multivariate convolutional neural network with error estimates to reconstruct sea surface temperature satellite and altimetry observations
paper.conclusion_note: All 23 B16 staging claims were checked against the hash-pinned published GMD paper. Seventeen claims are supported as written, five are only partially verified because they add an unstated characterization, combine distinct experiments, or combine separate problem statements, and one places an explicit 27-day input window under training.augmentation. This claim-set review is not a complete-paper attestation; the source code was not inspected and the 162-field contract was not reviewed field by field.

claims.extracted_value: Gap filling of satellite SST and along-track altimetry with per-pixel uncertainty
claims.evidence_summary: The abstract presents DINCAE as reconstruction of missing satellite data, applies it to gridded SST and along-track altimetry, and states that an error variance is produced per pixel and time instance.
claims.audit_note: The paper explicitly supports the combined high-level task and uncertainty output.

claims.evidence_summary: The authors describe an encoder-decoder DINCAE network and identify its general structure as a convolutional autoencoder and classical U-Net structure.
claims.audit_note: Both architecture-family labels are explicit in the primary paper.

claims.extracted_value: Convolutions and max pooling compress gappy observations plus metadata
claims.evidence_summary: The encoder receives gappy satellite observations with additional metadata and reduces their resolution through convolutional layers followed by max pooling.
claims.audit_note: The value preserves the reported inputs and encoder operations.

claims.extracted_value: Convolutions and interpolation reconstruct field and variance
claims.locator: Opening architecture paragraph; decoder implementation on p. 2187
claims.evidence_summary: The decoder reverses the encoder reduction using convolution and interpolation, and its final two channels are converted to the reconstruction and its error variance.
claims.audit_note: The decoder operations and both reported outputs are explicit.

claims.extracted_value: Addition-based skip connections and optional refinement network
claims.locator: Equation (2) and refinement description on p. 2185
claims.evidence_summary: DINCAE 2.0 implements sum-based skip connections and evaluates configurations with and without a second autoencoder refinement step.
claims.audit_note: Addition and the optional evaluated refinement configuration are both documented.

claims.extracted_value: Predicted field and expected error variance for each space-time pixel
claims.locator: Abstract output statement; Eq. (3) description on p. 2185
claims.evidence_summary: The article states that the network produces a reconstructed value and expected error variance for every pixel and time instance or grid cell.
claims.audit_note: The two outputs and their per-location scope are explicit.

claims.extracted_value: Gaussian negative log likelihood including residual scaled by predicted sigma and log variance
claims.evidence_summary: Equation (3) defines a Gaussian negative log-likelihood with squared residual divided by predicted variance and a log-variance penalty.
claims.audit_note: The stored description accurately summarizes the reported loss equation.

claims.extracted_value: Heteroscedastic Gaussian likelihood; predicts mean and variance
claims.evidence_summary: The authors explicitly define a Gaussian likelihood whose mean and variance are network outputs at each grid cell.
claims.audit_note: Mean and spatially varying variance are explicit, but the paper does not use the characterization 'heteroscedastic'; do not present that word as author terminology.

claims.extracted_value: Likelihood evaluated at valid non-masked observations
claims.locator: Equation (3), definition of the summation domain
claims.evidence_summary: The loss summation is explicitly restricted to grid points holding valid, non-masked values.
claims.audit_note: The masking behavior is directly stated.

claims.locator: Abstract multivariate example; dataset list on p. 2186
claims.evidence_summary: The multivariate SST experiment explicitly uses chlorophyll concentration and wind fields as auxiliary variables.
claims.audit_note: Both auxiliary-variable families are reported.

extracted_value: gappy SST and auxiliary fields OR irregular altimetry depending on experiment
claims.section: Abstract; 2.3 Multivariate reconstructions; 2.4 Non-gridded input data
claims.locator: Abstract experiment summary; input descriptions on p. 2185
claims.evidence_summary: The paper has a gridded SST experiment with auxiliary satellite fields and a distinct non-gridded along-track altimetry experiment.
claims.audit_note: The alternatives are supported, but they belong to distinct experiments and should not remain bound only to MAIN_EXPERIMENT.

claims.locator: Abstract applications and uncertainty output; Eq. (3) description on p. 2185
claims.evidence_summary: Each application produces a gridded reconstruction and predicted error variance, with SST and altimetry handled in separate experiments.
claims.audit_note: The values are supported, but the SST and altimetry outputs should retain their separate experiment scopes.

claims.evidence_summary: The authors state that all numerical experiments used the Adam optimizer.
claims.audit_note: Adam is explicitly reported and includes the altimetry case.

claims.evidence_summary: The reported batch contains 32 time instances.
claims.audit_note: The exact stored value and altimetry training context are supported.

claims.evidence_summary: The initial learning rate reported for Adam is 0.00058.
claims.audit_note: The exact stored learning rate is explicit.

claims.evidence_summary: The paper sets the L2 regularization coefficient on the weights to 10^-4.
claims.audit_note: The regularizer type and coefficient are explicit.

claims.evidence_summary: The absolute gradient value is clipped to 5 for training stability.
claims.audit_note: The exact clipping threshold is explicit.

claims.evidence_summary: The learning rate follows an exponential schedule controlled by gamma_decay and is halved every reciprocal-gamma_decay epochs.
claims.audit_note: The schedule form and control parameter are explicit.

claims.locator: Opening sentence continuing the input-window paragraph from p. 2188
claims.evidence_summary: The altimetry input uses tracks from a centered 27-day temporal window.
claims.audit_note: The value is explicit but is an input-window configuration, not data augmentation; move it to an input-history/window field without promoting this record.

claims.extracted_value: Supervised negative-log-likelihood with masked observations and cross-validation
claims.locator: Equation (3); data split on p. 2186; training and development-selection text on pp. 2188-2189
claims.evidence_summary: The paper defines Gaussian negative-log-likelihood on valid observations, separates training, development and test tracks, and tunes against development RMS.
claims.audit_note: The operational components are supported, but the paper does not label the method 'supervised' and the stored phrase collapses distinct loss, masking, split, and validation concepts.

claims.extracted_value: Hyperparameters selected by Bayesian optimization on development RMS
claims.evidence_summary: The authors determine the neural-network hyperparameters through Bayesian optimization that minimizes RMS error on the development dataset.
claims.audit_note: The method and selection objective are explicit.

claims.extracted_value: Ligurian Sea SST RMS decreases from 0.3835 C to 0.3604 C under new sum skip connection
claims.evidence_summary: For the Ligurian AVHRR test, the previous concatenation-skip RMS of 0.3835 degrees Celsius is reduced to 0.3604 with the new sum-skip approach.
claims.audit_note: Experiment, comparison, metric, units and values are explicit.

claims.extracted_value: Missing observations also affect the training samples; sparse irregular tracks require modified input/loss
claims.locator: Abstract problem statements and introduction discussion continuing on p. 2184
claims.evidence_summary: The authors state that missing or variable-accuracy data must be handled during training and call the regular-grid requirement of convolutional networks a limitation for irregularly sampled observations, motivating changes to the first layer and loss.
claims.audit_note: Both source-grounded issues are author reported, but the stored value combines the missing-training-data problem and the separate irregular-grid limitation into one claim.

unresolved: This is a review of the 23 imported B16 claims, not a complete field-by-field audit of the 162-field staging contract or the canonical PaperRecord.
The declared DINCAE.jl v2.0.0 author-code archive was not inspected or executed; no code-derived assertion or completeness attestation is made.
No separate scientific supplement is identified in the published article; no claim of exhaustive supplementary-material review is made beyond that source statement.
The gridded SST and non-gridded altimetry data.input_variables and data.output_variables claims need experiment-specific records rather than a single MAIN_EXPERIMENT binding.
training.augmentation is a field-path extraction defect: the 27-day value is an input temporal window. Add a regression case for temporal-window versus augmentation classification.
No NOT_REPORTED decision was made; establishing absence requires a separate documented full-scope search.
